news.full_article_text: Remarkable progress, but cancer won't be cured in the near future: Siddhartha Mukherjee at HTLS Oncologist and author Siddhartha Mukherjee said several cancers of the intestinal tract and the stomach "are really quite endemic" in India Cancer will not be cured in the near future, oncologist and author Siddhartha Mukherjee said on Saturday, even as he pointed to remarkable progress against some forms of the disease. In a conversation with HT’s Editor-in-Chief R Sukumar during the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit , Mukherjee spoke about how far humans understand life, how the rush to AI risks starving basic science in the US and India, where the line on gene editing should be drawn, and why science depends on agreeing on what words mean. On whether advances in immunotherapy, genetic sequencing and AI meant cancer could now be cured for sure, Mukherjee said: "We can say for sure we can't cure it. That I'm pretty sure about, at least in the near future." His explanation was the breadth of the challenge. "I think every cancer is different," he said. "We have made remarkable progress against, for instance, breast cancer, leukemias, lymphomas." A child with leukaemia whom he had treated with T-cell therapy in Bengaluru, and whose story he told in his talk, "is likely cured", he said. Several cancers of the intestinal tract and the stomach "are really quite endemic" in India, he said, "and I'm not sure that we can clearly foresee a cure for those in the near future". He called a recent drug against KRAS, a protein involved in pancreatic cancer, "a huge breakthrough". "But the idea that we will ever cure every cancer in sort of one fell swoop, I think, is just a mistaken idea." He was asked whether the focus on AI in medicine had come at the cost of fields such as cellular engineering and synthetic biology. Mukherjee said there were two answers —an intellectual one and a commercial one—and the commercial answer was "unfortunately, more relevant". Intellectually, the fields reinforce each other, he said: AI is helping cell therapy, immunotherapy and synthetic biology, and the collaboration between Immuneel, the Bengaluru cell-therapy company, and Manas AI, the drug-discovery company he co-founded, involves finding new binders between cells. Commercially, "when the pendulum swings and AI becomes fashionable", scientists who work on cell therapy are "led away" because "their grants can't get funded", he said. Scientific regulators need to "counterbalance the commercial forces" so that fields such as synthetic biology, fundamental chemistry, physics and biology "still remain funded". "And one of the great crises in this current administration is that the commercial has overrun the intellectual," he said of the US. "It's actually true for India too," he added. "When it becomes fashionable to talk about AI and becomes no longer fashionable to talk about fundamental chemistry or fundamental biology, we lose that balance and that has very long consequences." Mukherjee went back to Vannevar Bush, who shaped American science policy after the Second World War, and the idea that curiosity-driven basic science is the "bedrock" on which disciplines such as medicine are built. "If you disrupt the bedrock, obviously the consequences will be felt for everything," he said. Under "this current administration in the United States at least", he said, the commercial "has been allowed to overtake the bedrock". The consequences, he said, "are not felt in the five of years, but are felt in the tens of years". Asked where the line lies now that science can edit genes, Mukherjee pointed to a distinction he draws in his book, The Gene, between "human emancipation", by which he means the elimination of disease, and going beyond it. Most diseases do not depend on single genes, he said, and changing several genes, especially in a human embryo, is not easy. Some diseases are exceptions. "An important disease in India, for instance, sickle cell anemia, is actually very amenable to CRISPR-mediated technologies," he said. "There is a real possibility that you can enhance abilities," he said, such as parts of human anatomy, noting that a single gene controls much of human musculature. But there are "strong reasons to believe that CRISPR should not be used for that", he said, because it would divide people into "those who are able to access these technologies, and those who are unable to access these technologies". Asked whether a career spent telling the stories of genes, cells and cancer had changed his understanding of life, he said: "How could it not?" He added: "In science, history does not so much repeat itself as it reverberates." Science advances, he said, when people agree on the meaning of their terms: "The colloquial is the enemy of constructive debate." Mukherjee, who won the 2011 Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction for The Emperor of All Maladies, co-founded Manas AI in 2025 with LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman.

news.headline: Andhra Pradesh: Chainsaw attack accused shifted to Kurnool hospital after health worsens

news.full_article_text: Andhra Pradesh: Chainsaw attack accused shifted to Kurnool hospital after health worsens A police official said doctors at the Anantapur Government Hospital conducted several tests on Hemanth after he fell from his bed on the night of November 9 The police in Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district shifted 21-year-old Hemanth alias Dummu, accused of attacking a Class 10 girl with a chainsaw at the Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, to the Kurnool Government General Hospital on Friday night after his health deteriorated, police said on Saturday. A police official said doctors at the Anantapur Government Hospital conducted several tests on Hemanth after he fell from his bed on the night of November 9 and diagnosed him with pulmonary embolism, a potentially life-threatening condition involving blood clots in the blood vessels of the lungs. On Friday, the medical team at the Anantapur hospital submitted a status report to the state high court, stating that the blood clots in his blood vessels could pose a serious threat to his life if not treated immediately. The clots could travel to vital organs, including the heart, brain and lungs, potentially resulting in fatal complications, the report said. The medical team recommended shifting him to a higher medical facility, stating that although surgeons were available at the Anantapur hospital, it lacked the necessary infrastructure, including a heart-lung machine and other specialised facilities required to remove the clots. Also Read: AP chainsaw attack: HC seeks report on police firing at accused “Based on the medical report, the court permitted his transfer to the Kurnool government hospital. He was transported there in an Armed Reserve (AR) escort vehicle, accompanied by around 10 police personnel,” the police official said. Hemanth sustained bullet injuries when police opened fire on him on November 1 after he allegedly tried to escape, hours after being caught in the Atmakur forests. He was initially admitted to the Anantapur Government Hospital for treatment. However, complications arising from the gunshot injuries led to the amputation of his right leg around midnight on November 3, after blood circulation to the limb was disrupted. He also developed a bacterial infection that resulted in gangrene. Also Read: Andhra chainsaw attacker was teen victim’s uncle, harassed her in name of ‘love’: Police Despite continued medical treatment, his condition did not improve. He subsequently developed breathing difficulties, prompting doctors to conduct a CT scan on November 10. The scan reportedly revealed multiple small blood clots in his blood vessels, including those supplying the lungs, confirming pulmonary embolism. As he continued to experience serious respiratory complications, doctors concluded that he needed advanced treatment that was unavailable at the Anantapur hospital. Since Hemanth was being treated as a remand prisoner at the Anantapur hospital, the transfer procedure was completed through the Reddi Palli Jail. He was first taken from the hospital to the jail, where the necessary formalities were completed under the supervision of the jail authorities. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Srinivasa Rao Apparasu Srinivasa Rao is Senior Assistant Editor based out of Hyderabad covering developments in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana . He has over three decades of reporting experience.

news.headline: Amid Vidarbha drought, Gadkari pitches for MOIL and WCL mine water use for agricultural purposes
news.story_lead: Amid Vidarbha drought, Gadkari pitches for MOIL and WCL mine water use for agricultural purposes Nagpur, Union minister Nitin Gadkari on Saturday pitched for collective efforts for water conservation in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, and suggested that water from MOIL and WCL mines be provided to farmers for agricultural use. Speaking at the 17th Agrovision Agriculture Exhibition here, he said success stories of water conservation and groundwater recharge in Maharashtra's drought-affected regions will be presented at the event. At Agrovision, farmers can learn the stories of those who have successfully carried out water-conservation experiments, and undertake similar experiments in their own farms and villages, Gadkari added.
news.full_article_text: Amid Vidarbha drought, Gadkari pitches for MOIL and WCL mine water use for agricultural purposes Nagpur, Union minister Nitin Gadkari on Saturday pitched for collective efforts for water conservation in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, and suggested that water from MOIL and WCL mines be provided to farmers for agricultural use. Speaking at the 17th Agrovision Agriculture Exhibition here, he said success stories of water conservation and groundwater recharge in Maharashtra's drought-affected regions will be presented at the event. At Agrovision, farmers can learn the stories of those who have successfully carried out water-conservation experiments, and undertake similar experiments in their own farms and villages, Gadkari added. He is the chief patron of Agrovision. Emphasising the need for collective efforts for water conservation in every district of Vidarbha, he said discussions will be held on how this work can be carried out with even greater momentum to ensure Vidarbha becomes drought-free and irrigation can be expanded. Speaking about mine water for agricultural use, Gadkari said, "In Vidarbha, we have mines belonging to Manganese Ore India and WCL . Once those mines are excavated, water accumulates there." Gadkari urged state minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, who was present at the event, to invite representatives of MOIL and WCL to a major conference to be held in VNIT this December to discuss the issue. He said a paper had been prepared on such mine water, which can be supplied to farmers by installing solar pumps. It would be of considerable help in tiding over the drought situation, Gadkari said. "There are 6,500 malguzari lakes in Vidarbha. By deepening them, more water can be utilized. Furthermore, if the silt in dams is cleared, their usefulness can be increased," the Union minister added. Addressing a press conference, Gadkari also spoke about the Mankar Trust, which has 1600 teachers working with 40,000 tribal students. The work of the trust has been going on for 25 years, while he himself has worked on water issues for the last 26 years, he added. "As I have grown older, I say 'now call the young people' . news.exam_corner_topic: ‘No room for 7-hour sleep cycle’: Jaishankar shares glimpse into his diplomatic grind
news.headline: ‘No room for 7-hour sleep cycle’: Jaishankar shares glimpse into his diplomatic grind
news.story_lead: ‘No room for 7-hour sleep cycle’: Jaishankar shares glimpse into his diplomatic grind One cannot have a “24-hour life and a seven-hour sleep cycle”, Jaishankar said. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Saturday that he was “feeling good” even after seven years in a stressful job amid widespread geopolitical turbulence, and that he still tries to find time to relax by doing yoga, listening to music, or watching a movie. Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Jaishankar said that every day in his life “looks completely different because often, every day I'm in a completely different place”.
news.full_article_text: ‘No room for 7-hour sleep cycle’: Jaishankar shares glimpse into his diplomatic grind One cannot have a “24-hour life and a seven-hour sleep cycle”, Jaishankar said. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Saturday that he was “feeling good” even after seven years in a stressful job amid widespread geopolitical turbulence, and that he still tries to find time to relax by doing yoga, listening to music, or watching a movie. Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Jaishankar said that every day in his life “looks completely different because often, every day I'm in a completely different place”. This requires him to adjust his schedule continuously to meet the demands of the situation. “I am feeling good,” he replied when he was asked how he felt after seven years in a stressful job. Deep Dive Jaishankar, who has made 161 foreign trips since he became foreign minister in 2019, including 23 in 2026, said: “Every day looks completely different because often, every day I'm in a completely different place. I think today if you're an active foreign minister, in this very turbulent era…it means a lot of travel, but it also means a lot of time zones.” One cannot have a “24-hour life and a seven-hour sleep cycle”, he said. “You have no time; you adjust your day continuously to the requirements of the situation, you build it into your life. I try to handle the travel, and getting up at night and doing your phone calls and going back to sleep and staying abreast of everything that's happening,” he added. Besides handling his duties related to foreign policy, he also has to do everything required of a cabinet minister at home. While doing all of this, he attempts to build elements of personal comfort into his routine. “So, you try to stay physically fit, you try to do something to relax yourself. I do yoga regularly, I listen to music occasionally, try to watch a movie, definitely read a book. I do all the normal things,” Jaishankar said. - External Affairs Minister

news.headline: US went easy on Pakistan’s military for years, says Blinken at HT Leadership Summit
news.story_lead: US went easy on Pakistan’s military for years, says Blinken at HT Leadership Summit Blinken drew a sharp line between the two relationships. India, he said, was a global force, while the relationship with Pakistan “has been regional”. Former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken on Saturday said Washington’s need for Pakistan’s help in Afghanistan had probably made it less critical of the military’s grip on Pakistan’s government.
news.full_article_text: US went easy on Pakistan’s military for years, says Blinken at HT Leadership Summit Blinken drew a sharp line between the two relationships. India, he said, was a global force, while the relationship with Pakistan “has been regional”. Former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken on Saturday said Washington’s need for Pakistan’s help in Afghanistan had probably made it less critical of the military’s grip on Pakistan’s government. He said the US no longer views India through a Pakistan lens. “Seeing the relationship with India in some fashion through the prism of Pakistan, that is over and done,” Blinken said at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit. He said the earlier approach was driven by expedience, mainly the US’s goals in Afghanistan, and that this had ended, allowing Washington to recalibrate. He drew a sharp line between the two relationships. India, he said, was a global force, while the relationship with Pakistan “has been regional”. “These are fundamentally different relationships,” he said. Deep Dive On terrorism, Blinken said the US had “zero tolerance”. He said Washington must respect India’s right to defend itself when attacked, and also back the diplomatic efforts needed to deal with that challenge. He acknowledged that Washington’s past dealings with Pakistan had come at a cost. That expedience “probably caused us to have less of a critical hand when it comes to the government, the military, the civil-military balance,” he said. “There is an opportunity for the United States to do more to try to see that balance change.” But he said the US could not impose an outcome. “These are decisions that Pakistanis make about the nature of their society, the nature of their governments, and it’s not going to be done by us or by anyone else. We can be very supportive, but these are fundamentally decisions that Pakistanis make.” He said he hoped the subcontinent would eventually be “integrated in the most positive way”. He described Pakistan as “a shadow” on India-US ties, and raised two concerns: the role of the Pakistani military in terrorism, and how civil-military imbalance undermines democracy in Pakistan. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. bullet_points: US went easy on Pakistan’s military for years, says Blinken at HT Leadership Summit
Blinken drew a sharp line between the two relationships. India, he said, was a global force, while the relationship with Pakistan “has been regional”.

Former US Secretary of State Antony Blinken on Saturday said Washington’s need for Pakistan’s help in Afghanistan had probably made it less critical of the military’s grip on Pakistan’s government. He said the US no longer views India through a Pakistan lens.

“Seeing the relationship with India in some fashion through the prism of Pakistan, that is over and done,” Blinken said at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit. He said the earlier approach was driven by expedience, mainly the US’s goals in Afghanistan, and that this had ended, allowing Washington to recalibrate.

He drew a sharp line between the two relationships. India, he said, was a global force, while the relationship with Pakistan “has been regional”. “These are fundamentally different relationships,” he said.

On terrorism, Blinken said the US had “zero tolerance”. He said Washington must respect India’s right to defend itself when attacked, and also back the diplomatic efforts needed to deal with that challenge.

He acknowledged that Washington’s past dealings with Pakistan had come at a cost. That expedience “probably caused us to have less of a critical hand when it comes to the government, the military, the civil-military balance,” he said. “There is an opportunity for the United States to do more to try to see that balance change.”

But he said the US could not impose an outcome. “These are decisions that Pakistanis make about the nature of their society, the nature of their governments, and it’s not going to be done by us or by anyone else. We can be very supportive, but these are fundamentally decisions that Pakistanis make.”

news.headline: New world order will be more multipolar and transactional: Jaishankar at HT Leadership Summit
news.story_lead: New world order will be more multipolar and transactional: Jaishankar at HT Leadership Summit Jaishankar said this new order is taking shape at a time when the world is navigating “very stormy seas" amid multiple conflicts. The new world order taking shape will be more multipolar and transactional, with more centres of autonomous decision-making, thereby making it more unstable and setting the stage for sharper competition, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Saturday. Speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Jaishankar said this new order is taking shape at a time when the world is navigating “very stormy seas” because of multiple conflicts, including those in Ukraine and West Asia, the grim situation in parts of Africa, and disruptions and volatility in food and fuel supplies.
news.full_article_text: New world order will be more multipolar and transactional: Jaishankar at HT Leadership Summit Jaishankar said this new order is taking shape at a time when the world is navigating “very stormy seas" amid multiple conflicts. The new world order taking shape will be more multipolar and transactional, with more centres of autonomous decision-making, thereby making it more unstable and setting the stage for sharper competition, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Saturday. Speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Jaishankar said this new order is taking shape at a time when the world is navigating “very stormy seas” because of multiple conflicts, including those in Ukraine and West Asia, the grim situation in parts of Africa, and disruptions and volatility in food and fuel supplies. “The general acceptance is that the new order would be more multipolar, that there’d be many more centres of autonomous decision-making. Countries overall would be much more national in their choices and in their decisions,” he said in a conversation with HT's Editor-In-Chief R Sukumar. Deep Dive “The alliances will be less cohesive because of national interests and more transactional, because they feed into each other — less cohesive, more transactional; more transactional, less cohesive.” The new world order will also be one of “more variables”, and “much more complex [and] less predictable” because there are more players, who are also more self-centered. “That will be the culture or the ethos of the era that we are moving into. I don’t want you to get a sort of picture of an anarchy, but definitely sharper competition, more national assertions, and in that sense inherently more unstable,” Jaishankar said. Jaishankar acknowledged that the world was “in a mess” and charting “very stormy seas”, with global headwinds having consequences for India. The changes underway have been exacerbated by the wars in Ukraine and West Asia, the grim situation in Sudan and Central Africa, the volatility of food and fuel prices, and the continuing fallout of the Covid-19 pandemic, he said. “Five years ago, it would have been inconceivable in this day and age, when everything is so globalised and interdependent, that we could have a major war. We’ve actually had that war now into its fifth year,” he said, referring to the Russia-Ukraine conflict. “What you see in the Gulf — the idea that countries would actually be firing missiles at each other, targeting bases, cities, forces, leaderships — would have been something which people would have rated its chances as pretty near zero,” he said, adding that the situation in West Asia had become “much more bitter and intractable” since the terror attacks by Hamas in October 2023. Food exports from Ukraine and Russia were stuck in the Black Sea, impacting global food prices, including those in India, while fuel prices too were rising because of disruptions, he said. Tackling these challenges requires strong, steady and experienced leadership that “knows how to get the country through this, because the compass for navigating it is our national interest”, Jaishankar said. “When we look at all these challenges, when people ask us where do you stand on Ukraine or where do you stand on the Gulf or what is your view on a particular challenge, we will view it understandably through the lens of our national interest. That’s the compass which will guide us,” he said, adding this turbulence will show up in different ways till the end of the current decade. The turbulence on the global stage is being driven by multiple causes, though US-China competition is a “big part of the overall…disturbance or volatility”, Jaishankar said. “One part of it is when countries get caught up in between, but it’s also led to the US itself changing the manner in which it approaches the world,” he said. The changes underway have acquired a greater degree of sharpness amid the US-China competition and a marked change in Washington’s approach towards even its long-standing partners. The US’s focus on reindustrialising to ensure it isn’t excessively dependent on a particular country or geography has also led to vulnerability. “One part of it is to look at a US-China competition in a very orthodox way. But if you look at it more deeply…each one of these feeds into the other and a big part of it is really the changed approach of the US to the world, even to its friends and allies,” Jaishankar said. The US was politically dominant in the world order put in place after World War II because it was willing to underwrite economic arrangements as they served American interests. But things changed, going back to the term of former president Joe Biden, as the US found that the rules “it was underwriting had been gamed to its disadvantage”, he pointed out. “The US, which was a big energy importer from the Gulf, today is self-sufficient and an energy exporter. If it was an energy importer today, I’m not sure many of the events which are happening in the Gulf would still be happening,” Jaishankar said. As the energy scenario has significantly changed, technology gaps have grown, and there has been a revolution in warfare, the political atmosphere has led to greater propensity to take risks. “It’s a more competitive word, it’s also a much more risk-taking word, and not limited to the US,” Jaishankar said. “Other players are also taking risks. Everybody is pushing the envelope [and] the more powerful are able to push the envelope much stronger and on many more issues.” With the world in a transitional phase, there is an expectation that the new order will have a “much stronger role of India or much stronger influence by India”, Jaishankar said. This will require stronger domestic capacities, including through initiatives such as Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India), Make in India and Innovate in India, which are the building blocks of foreign policy. At the same time, India will have to reforge relationships, diversify and de-risk. “In the last decade, we have laid a very solid foundation…with this very strong push for industrialisation because…we missed the manufacturing bus. That for us, [from] the 1960s to the end of the 1990s, we may have had reform, but these were really lost decades. Even the reform was only a correction and a partial correction of what were lost decades before 1992,” he said. static_gk: National Investigation Agency (NIA): Established under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008, functioning as the central counter-terrorism law enforcement agency under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Assam Rifles: Formed in 1835 as Cachar Levy, it is India's oldest paramilitary force, operating under the administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs and operational control of the Indian Army.
National Highway 202 (NH 202): Connects Imphal in Manipur with Nagaland via Ukhrul.
news.headline: Manipur Chief Minister Convenes High-Level Security Review Following Violence in Kangpokpi and Ukhrul
news.story_lead: Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand presided over a high-level security meeting at the Chief Minister's Secretariat in Imphal following a fresh outbreak of violence that left five individuals dead across two districts. The state leadership ordered intensive combing operations and reinforced troop deployments across vulnerable regions, while local ethnic bodies issued strict ultimatums to the administration.
news.full_article_text:
### High-Level Security Review Meeting

Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand chaired an emergency security assessment meeting at the Cabinet Hall of the Chief Minister’s Secretariat in Babupara, Imphal. The meeting was convened to evaluate the deteriorating law and order situation following two lethal attacks in Kangpokpi and Ukhrul districts.

### Key Security Decisions

- **Sustained Combing Operations:** Security forces were instructed to execute continuous search and combing operations across affected areas to apprehend perpetrators involved in recent armed attacks.
- **Strengthening Post Jurisdiction:** Deployment at all existing security outposts will be fortified, directing personnel to heighten surveillance and defense within their respective territorial jurisdictions.
- **Vulnerable Zone Protection:** Specialized security measures were drawn up to protect sensitive and vulnerable civilian zones across the state.

### Leadership & Agency Participation

The strategic meeting included key state officials and central security agency leaders:
- **State Officials:** Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam, Chief Secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur, Security Advisor Kuldiep Singh, DGP Mukesh Singh, and the ADGP (Law and Order).
- **Central Forces Representation:** Senior commanders from the Assam Rifles, Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Border Security Force (BSF), and intelligence officials from central agencies.

### Overview of Recent Incidents

Five fatalities occurred over two consecutive days in separate district incidents:
- **Taphou Kuki Village Incident (Kangpokpi District):** On Thursday, a 40-year-old Kuki woman, identified as Kimneineng Chongloi, was shot and killed while working in a paddy field during an armed attack.
- **New Heaven Village Ambush (Ukhrul District):** On Friday, an ambush along National Highway 202 (connecting Imphal to Nagaland via Ukhrul) resulted in the deaths of four Naga civilians, allegedly carried out by armed insurgents.

### Ultimatums by Local Civil Society Organisations

- **Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL) Demands:** The Naga organisation issued a 3-day public ultimatum demanding the expulsion of insurgent groups from Naga-inhabited areas and requesting an immediate transfer of the investigation to the National Investigation Agency (NIA). Citing this as the fourth attack at the same location, TNL demanded the withdrawal of central security forces and threatened an indefinite agitation if demands are unmet.
- **Kuki Inpi Manipur (KIM) Demands:** The Kuki organisation issued a 72-hour ultimatum to the Manipur Police, accusing them of institutional bias and selective reporting regarding the official descriptions of the attacks. KIM demanded an internal inquiry, public explanation, and corrective action, warning of legal recourse and non-cooperation with police in Kuki-dominated areas.

hindi_translation.headline: कांगपोकपी और उखरुल में हिंसा के बाद मणिपुर के मुख्यमंत्री ने उच्च स्तरीय सुरक्षा समीक्षा बैठक की अध्यक्षता की
hindi_translation.story_lead: मणिपुर के मुख्यमंत्री युमनाम खेमचंद ने दो जिलों में पांच लोगों की मौत के बाद इम्फाल स्थित मुख्यमंत्री सचिवालय में उच्च स्तरीय सुरक्षा बैठक की अध्यक्षता की। राज्य नेतृत्व ने संवेदनशील क्षेत्रों में तलाशी अभियान तेज करने और सुरक्षा बलों की तैनाती मजबूत करने का निर्देश दिया, जबकि स्थानीय जातीय संगठनों ने प्रशासन को अल्टीमेटम जारी किया है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### उच्च स्तरीय सुरक्षा समीक्षा बैठक

मणिपुर के मुख्यमंत्री युमनाम खेमचंद ने बाबूपाड़ा, इम्फाल स्थित मुख्यमंत्री सचिवालय के कैबिनेट हॉल में आपातकालीन सुरक्षा समीक्षा बैठक की अध्यक्षता की। यह बैठक कांगपोकपी और उखरुल जिलों में हुई दो हिंसक घटनाओं के बाद कानून-व्यवस्था की समीक्षा के लिए बुलाई गई थी।

### प्रमुख सुरक्षा निर्णय

- **सघन तलाशी अभियान:** सुरक्षा बलों को निर्देश दिया गया है कि वे हालिया हमलों में शामिल अपराधियों को पकड़ने के लिए प्रभावित क्षेत्रों में तलाशी अभियान जारी रखें।
- **सुरक्षा चौकियों की मजबूती:** विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में तैनात सुरक्षा कर्मियों को अपने-अपने अधिकार क्षेत्रों में सुरक्षा व्यवस्था मजबूत करने के निर्देश दिए गए।
- **संवेदनशील क्षेत्रों की सुरक्षा:** राज्य के संवेदनशील और अति-संवेदनशील नागरिक क्षेत्रों की सुरक्षा के लिए विशेष उपाय तैयार किए गए।

### प्रमुख अधिकारियों एवं एजेंसियों की भागीदारी

रणनीतिक बैठक में राज्य के वरिष्ठ अधिकारियों और केंद्रीय सुरक्षा एजेंसियों के प्रमुखों ने भाग लिया:
- **राज्य प्रतिनिधि:** गृह मंत्री गोविंददास कोंथौजम, मुख्य सचिव राजीव सिंह ठाकुर, सुरक्षा सलाहकार कुलदीप सिंह, पुलिस महानिदेशक (DGP) मुकेश सिंह और एडीजीपी (कानून और व्यवस्था)।
- **केंद्रीय बल प्रतिनिधि:** असम राइफल्स, केंद्रीय रिजर्व पुलिस बल (CRPF), सीमा सुरक्षा बल (BSF) और केंद्रीय खुफिया एजेंसियों के वरिष्ठ अधिकारी।

### हालिया घटनाओं का विवरण

पिछले दो दिनों में दो अलग-अलग घटनाओं में पांच लोगों की जान गई है:
- **ताफू कुकी गांव घटना (कांगपोकपी जिला):** गुरुवार को 40 वर्षीय कुकी महिला किम्नेइनेन्ग चोंगलोई की धान के खेत में काम करते समय सशस्त्र हमले में गोली मारकर हत्या कर दी गई।
- **न्यू हेवन गांव घात लगाकर हमला (उखरुल जिला):** शुक्रवार को राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 202 (इम्फाल-नागालैंड वाया उखरुल) पर न्यू हेवन गांव के पास घात लगाकर किए गए हमले में चार नागा नागरिकों की मौत हो गई।

### स्थानीय नागरिक निकायों का अल्टीमेटम

- **तांगखुल नागा लोंग (TNL) की मांगें:** नागा संगठन ने राज्य और केंद्र सरकार को 3 दिन का अल्टीमेटम दिया, जिसमें नागा क्षेत्रों से उग्रवादी समूहों को बाहर निकालने और मामले की जांच राष्ट्रीय जांच एजेंसी (NIA) को सौंपने की मांग की गई है।
- **कुकी इनपी मणिपुर (KIM) की मांगें:** कुकी संगठन ने मणिपुर पुलिस को 72 घंटे का अल्टीमेटम जारी किया, जिसमें पुलिस पर घटनाओं की पक्षपातपूर्ण रिपोर्टिंग का आरोप लगाया गया और आंतरिक जांच व स्पष्टीकरण की मांग की गई।

news.headline: Assam Chief Minister Orders Probe into Golaghat Road Accident, Announces Strict Enforcement of Traffic Regulations
news.story_lead: Following a fatal collision in Assam's Golaghat district near Kaziranga that claimed 26 lives, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced a high-level investigation and a complete reversal of recent traffic rule relaxations. The state government pledged ₹7 lakh in ex-gratia compensation alongside ₹2 lakh from the central government, promising strict action against speeding, vehicle overcrowding, and safety tampering.
news.full_article_text:
### Assam Reinstates Strict Traffic Enforcement After Tragic Golaghat Crash

Following a head-on collision between a minibus and a truck near Kaziranga in Golaghat district that resulted in 26 fatalities, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma ordered a comprehensive inquiry into the incident. Visiting the accident site on Saturday, the Chief Minister publicly acknowledged that previous relaxations in traffic rules—decided during a Cabinet meeting in Nalbari due to political pressure—were erroneous. He committed to reinstating rigorous traffic enforcement across the state to prioritize public safety over political expediency.

### Vehicle Violations and Investigation Details

According to briefings provided by Golaghat Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Swapnaneel Deka, the involved minibus (a Force Traveller) exhibited severe safety and regulatory compliance failures:

- **Overloading:** The 27-seater minibus was carrying 41 passengers at the time of the crash. It initially departed Golaghat with eight passengers around noon and picked up numerous passengers, including students, along the route between Bokakhat and Kohora.
- **Tampered Speed-Limiting Device (SLD):** Although transport records indicated an active SLD set at 80 km/h, the device had been manually disconnected by the driver. The speed limit on the Kaziranga stretch is restricted to 40 km/h.
- **Speeding Evidence:** Retracted dashcam footage reviewed by officials and police indicated the vehicle was traveling at an estimated speed exceeding 120 km/h in clear road conditions.
- **Past Enforcement Records:** Official transport records revealed the minibus had 12 paid traffic challans amounting to ₹38,500, with an additional ₹4,000 pending. On March 3, the vehicle was cited in Jorhat for driving at 102 km/h.
- **Driver Profile and Mechanical Failure:** The 64-year-old driver died in the crash. Authorities suspect a possible sudden medical event, such as a stroke, alongside poor brake conditions, which will be confirmed via post-mortem reports.

### Financial Relief and Statewide Compliance Crackdown

To support the victims' families, the Assam government announced an ex-gratia payment of ₹7 lakh per deceased individual, supplementing the ₹2 lakh compensation declared by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from the central fund, bringing total financial relief to ₹9 lakh per family. 

Highlighting a noticeable rise in road traffic fatalities over the past two to three years, the Chief Minister outlined a statewide crackdown targeting:
1. Overloading of commercial and passenger transport.
2. Speeding and bypassing of SLDs.
3. Drunk driving and non-compliance with helmet/seatbelt mandates.
4. Operation of fitness-uncertified vehicles.

### Victim Profile and Demographics

The deceased comprised 14 women, 12 men, including a child. The victims spanned multiple districts, including 10 from Golaghat, 12 from Nagaon, 1 from Karbi Anglong, 1 from Sonitpur, and 1 resident of Madhubani, Bihar, while one victim at Jorhat Medical College and Hospital (JMCH) remained unidentified.

news.upsc_analysis: The Golaghat tragedy highlights systemic failures in road safety enforcement in India, demonstrating how technical interventions like Speed Limiting Devices (SLDs) are rendered ineffective without continuous physical and digital oversight. The Chief Minister's admission regarding regulatory relaxations under political pressure underscores the policy dilemma between strict regulatory compliance and local administrative compromises. Achieving the goal of reducing road traffic fatalities requires institutionalizing automated enforcement networks, mandatory periodic driver health evaluations, stringent hardware anti-tampering laws, and removing administrative discretion in traffic penalty enforcement.

news.mains_notes:
### Road Safety Governance and Enforcement Architecture

- **Regulatory Enforcement Gaps:** The Golaghat crash illustrates how non-compliance, hardware tampering (SLDs), and systemic overloading persist despite statutory mandates under the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019.
- **Political Economy of Regulation:** Ad-hoc relaxations in enforcement due to localized political demands compromise public safety, creating regulatory moral hazard.
- **Multi-Pronged Intervention Strategy:**
  1. *Technological Integration:* Automated Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) and tamper-proof electronic speed governors.
  2. *Strict Driver Assessment:* Age-tiered medical fitness certifications for commercial transport operators.
  3. *Zero-Tolerance Policy:* Automated escalation of penalties for repeat offenders with multiple challans.

Regulatory compromise under political pressure often compromises public safety infrastructure. Analyze this statement in the context of traffic safety enforcement and suggest reformative measures.

hindi_translation.headline: असम के मुख्यमंत्री ने गोलाघाट सड़क हादसे की जांच के आदेश दिए, यातायात नियमों को सख्त करने का संकल्प लिया
hindi_translation.story_lead: गोलाघाट जिले में काजीरंगा के पास एक मिनीबस और ट्रक की सीधी भिड़ंत में 26 लोगों की मौत के बाद, असम के मुख्यमंत्री हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा ने विस्तृत जांच के आदेश दिए हैं और यातायात नियमों में दी गई ढील को वापस लेने की घोषणा की है। राज्य सरकार ने मृतकों के परिजनों को 7 लाख रुपये तथा केंद्र सरकार ने 2 लाख रुपये की अनुग्रह राशि देने का ऐलान किया है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### गोलाघाट हादसे के बाद असम सरकार सख्त यातायात नियम लागू करेगी

असम के गोलाघाट जिले में काजीरंगा के पास एक मिनीबस और ट्रक के बीच हुई दर्दनाक दुर्घटना में 26 लोगों की मौत के बाद मुख्यमंत्री हिमंत बिस्वा सरमा ने विस्तृत जांच का निर्देश दिया है। शनिवार को दुर्घटनास्थल का दौरा करने के बाद मुख्यमंत्री ने स्वीकार किया कि राजनीतिक दबाव के कारण नलबाड़ी कैबिनेट बैठक में यातायात नियमों में दी गई ढील एक गलत निर्णय था। उन्होंने स्पष्ट किया कि जनसुरक्षा को प्राथमिकता देते हुए कड़े नियमों को पुन: लागू किया जाएगा।

### वाहन उल्लंघनों और जांच के मुख्य तथ्य

गोलाघाट के वरिष्ठ पुलिस अधीक्षक (एसएसपी) स्वप्ननील डेका द्वारा दी गई जानकारी के अनुसार:

- **अत्यधिक सवारी (ओवरलोडिंग):** 27 सीटों वाली मिनीबस में 41 यात्री सवार थे। यह बस दोपहर लगभग 12 बजे गोलाघाट से 8 यात्रियों के साथ चली थी और बोकाखाट से कोहोरा के बीच कई छात्रों सहित अन्य यात्रियों को बैठाया गया।
- **स्पीड गवर्नर से छेड़छाड़:** आधिकारिक रिकॉर्ड में वाहन में 80 किमी/घंटा का स्पीड-लिमिटिंग डिवाइस (SLD) दर्ज था, लेकिन ड्राइवर ने इसे काट दिया था। काजीरंगा वाले मार्ग पर गति सीमा 40 किमी/घंटा निर्धारित है।
- **अत्यधिक गति के प्रमाण:** डैशकैम फुटेज की समीक्षा से पता चला कि दुर्घटना के समय वाहन की गति 120 किमी/घंटा से अधिक थी।
- **पुराना चालान रिकॉर्ड:** परिवहन विभाग के रिकॉर्ड के अनुसार वाहन पर 38,500 रुपये के 12 चालान भुगतान किए जा चुके थे, जबकि 4,000 रुपये लंबित थे। 3 मार्च को जोरहाट में इस वाहन का 102 किमी/घंटा की गति से चलने पर चालान किया गया था।
- **चालक की स्थिति:** 64 वर्षीय चालक की भी दुर्घटना में मृत्यु हो गई। पुलिस को आशंका है कि संभवतः चालक को अचानक स्ट्रोक या अन्य कोई चिकित्सा समस्या हुई होगी, जिसकी पुष्टि पोस्टमार्टम रिपोर्ट से होगी।

### वित्तीय सहायता और राज्यव्यापी कार्रवाई

मृतकों के परिवारों को सहायता प्रदान करने के लिए राज्य सरकार ने 7 लाख रुपये तथा केंद्र सरकार ने 2 लाख रुपये की सहायता राशि की घोषणा की है, जिससे कुल मुआवजा 9 लाख रुपये हो गया है। मुख्यमंत्री ने बताया कि पिछले 2-3 वर्षों में राज्य में सड़क दुर्घटनाओं में वृद्धि हुई है, जिसे रोकने के लिए ओवरलोडिंग, ओवर-स्पीडिंग, शराब पीकर गाड़ी चलाने और बिना फिटनेस वाले वाहनों के खिलाफ सख्त अभियान चलाया जाएगा।
hindi_translation.background_context: असम सरकार ने पूर्व में राजनीतिक दबाव के चलते नलबाड़ी कैबिनेट बैठक में यातायात नियमों में कुछ ढील दी थी। राज्य में पिछले 2-3 वर्षों से सड़क दुर्घटनाओं में मौतों का आंकड़ा बढ़ रहा था।
bullet_points: असम के मुख्यमंत्री ने गोलाघाट जिले में 26 लोगों की जान लेने वाले सड़क हादसे की विस्तृत जांच के आदेश दिए।
नलबाड़ी कैबिनेट बैठक के दौरान यातायात नियमों में दी गई ढील को रद्द कर सख्त नियम पुन: लागू करने की घोषणा की गई।
मृतकों के परिवारों के लिए कुल 9 लाख रुपये (राज्य सरकार से 7 लाख रुपये और केंद्र से 2 लाख रुपये) का मुआवजा घोषित किया गया।
27-सीटर मिनीबस में क्षमता से अधिक 41 यात्री सवार थे।
जांच में पाया गया कि ड्राइवर ने स्पीड-लिमिटिंग डिवाइस (SLD) को हटा दिया था।
डैशकैम फुटेज के अनुसार वाहन 40 किमी/घंटा की निर्धारित सीमा वाले क्षेत्र में 120 किमी/घंटा से अधिक की गति से चल रहा था।
वाहन पर पूर्व में 12 चालान (₹38,500) का भुगतान हो चुका था और ₹4,000 का चालान लंबित था।
ओवरलोडिंग, ओवर-स्पीडिंग और सुरक्षा उपकरणों की अनदेखी पर राज्यव्यापी सख्त कार्रवाई शुरू की जाएगी।
key_facts: दुर्घटना में कुल मौतें: 26 (14 महिलाएं, 12 पुरुष, जिनमें 1 बच्चा शामिल)।
वाहन क्षमता बनाम सवारियां: 27 सीटों वाली बस में 41 यात्री।
काजीरंगा क्षेत्र की गति सीमा: 40 किमी/घंटा; अनुमानित गति: >120 किमी/घंटा।
कुल अनुग्रह राशि: ₹7 लाख (राज्य) + ₹2 लाख (केंद्र) = ₹9 लाख प्रति परिवार।
important_dates: 2026-11-14 (मुख्यमंत्री का दौरा और नीतिगत घोषणाएं)

news.headline: Mumbai Youth Arrested for Conducting Surveillance on Sensitive Locations for Foreign Criminal Syndicates
news.story_lead: A 20-year-old resident of Airoli, Navi Mumbai, was apprehended after being discovered conducting reconnaissance on high-profile sensitive locations in South Mumbai, including Chabad House. The suspect was acting under the instructions of overseas criminal networks and anti-national elements contacted via messaging platforms. Following initial detention by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), he was formally taken into custody by Keralam Police in connection with a UAPA case.
news.full_article_text:
A joint security operation led to the arrest of a 20-year-old man, identified as Yash Singh, for allegedly carrying out surveillance and photographing sensitive installations across South Mumbai. Initial intelligence gathered by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) flagged his social media interactions with handlers associated with foreign criminal networks and anti-national entities. Following questioning, Singh was handed over to and formally arrested by the Keralam Police, as his activities were linked to an ongoing investigation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) registered at the Thrissur East police station.

According to official statements, Singh was tasked by online handlers—linked to international mafia cartels such as the Pakistan-based 'Shahzad Bhatti Network'—to conduct reconnaissance in strategic commercial and cultural hubs around Colaba in South Mumbai. His specific assignments entailed photographing, geotagging, and mapping key locations, primarily targeting Chabad House, businesses owned by Jewish citizens, and locations frequently visited by foreign tourists. He reportedly received financial remuneration for supplying these intelligence inputs.

Investigation revealed that communication was maintained primarily through encrypted messaging channels like Telegram. Transnational criminal networks have increasingly leveraged platforms like Telegram, Instagram, and WhatsApp to target unemployed or financially vulnerable youth, enticing them with monetary incentives to execute local intelligence gathering and disruptive activities. The ATS issued an advisory urging citizens and parents to monitor online activities, avoid communicating with unknown entities, and refrain from sharing sensitive location data online.
news.background_context: Chabad House, located in Colaba, South Mumbai, was one of the key locations targeted by Pakistani terrorists during the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks (26/11).
bullet_points: A 20-year-old Navi Mumbai resident, Yash Singh, was arrested for conducting surveillance on key sensitive sites in Mumbai.
The suspect targeted Jewish-owned businesses, foreign national hotspots, and Chabad House in Colaba.
Initial action was taken by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) based on social media monitoring.
He was subsequently taken into custody by Keralam Police under a UAPA case registered in Thrissur district.
Overseas criminal entities, including the Pakistan-based 'Shahzad Bhatti Network', reportedly directed the operation.
Encrypted messaging platforms such as Telegram, Instagram, and WhatsApp were used for communication and recruitment.
The suspect received financial payment in exchange for detailed photographs and location data of sensitive targets.
Law enforcement authorities issued an advisory urging vigilance against online recruitment targeting vulnerable youth.
key_facts: Suspect Name: Yash Singh (20 years old, resident of Airoli, Navi Mumbai).
Primary Target: Chabad House, Colaba (previously targeted during the 26/11 attacks in 2008).
Investigating Agencies: Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Keralam Police (Thrissur East police station).
Applicable Law: Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).
Network Involved: Foreign syndicate identified as 'Shahzad Bhatti Network' operating from Pakistan.
Communication Channels Used: Telegram, Instagram, WhatsApp.
important_dates: 2008: Chabad House targeted during 26/11 Mumbai terrorist attacks.
2026-11-14: Formal announcement of the arrest and transfer to Keralam Police.
exam_relevance: UPSC GS Paper III: Internal Security threats, role of non-state actors, cross-border crime syndicates, and radicalisation via social media/encrypted messaging apps.
Prelims: Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) provisions, functions of state Anti-Terrorism Squads (ATS).
news.upsc_analysis: The case highlights the evolving threat matrix where cross-border terrorist and criminal syndicates hybridise their operations. By utilizing social media and encrypted messaging platforms (Telegram, WhatsApp, Instagram), foreign anti-national elements weaponise unemployed youth for proxy surveillance. This hybrid threat model combines organized crime with terrorist logistics, requiring proactive cyber-intelligence and inter-state police coordination.
causes: Use of encrypted social media channels by overseas criminal cartels to exploit financially vulnerable or unemployed youth.
Cross-border planning aimed at targeting high-value, sensitive infrastructure and foreign nationals in India.
impacts: Heightened security alerts around vulnerable religious and economic infrastructure in South Mumbai.
Inter-state police coordination resulting in the enforcement of strict anti-terror legislation (UAPA).
challenges: Tracing end-to-end encrypted communication networks operated from foreign jurisdictions.
Preventing online recruitment and radicalisation/monetary exploitation of young citizens.
government_steps: Inter-agency coordination between Maharashtra ATS and Keralam Police.
Registration of cases under the stringent Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).
Public advisories issued by ATS targeting youth online safety and cyber awareness.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), 1967 - Framework for combating unlawful activities and terrorism in India.
Seventh Schedule of the Constitution - 'Public Order' and 'Police' as State subjects, requiring seamless inter-state intelligence sharing.
way_forward: Strengthen cyber-surveillance and social media monitoring mechanisms to disrupt online recruitment pipelines.
Enhance inter-state coordination between state Anti-Terrorism Squads and central intelligence agencies.
Conduct grassroots awareness programs to prevent vulnerable youth from falling prey to financial enticements by subversive networks.
news.mains_notes:
Key Themes: Internal Security, Cross-Border Cyber Networks, UAPA Case Study.
- Hybrid Threats: Criminal syndicates acting as force multipliers for terrorist planning.
- Method of Recruitment: Exploitation of vulnerable youth via social media platforms for monetary gains.
- Legal Provisions: UAPA applied due to direct nexus with anti-national acts and security threats.
- Countermeasure: Need for robust cyber intelligence, inter-state operational synergy, and public awareness campaigns.
mains_questions: Examine how cross-border criminal networks utilize social media and encrypted messaging platforms to undermine India's internal security. Suggest effective policy measures to mitigate this threat.
Discuss the challenges in inter-state intelligence sharing and law enforcement coordination while investigating cases under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).
news.takeaway: A 20-year-old man was arrested in Mumbai for conducting reconnaissance of sensitive locations like Chabad House under the instructions of a foreign criminal network, underscoring the growing use of social media platforms for proxy anti-national activities.
prelims_facts: Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) allows prosecution for acts threatening the sovereignty and integrity of India.
Chabad House in Colaba, Mumbai, was one of the sites attacked during the 2008 26/11 terror attacks.
The Shahzad Bhatti Network is an overseas criminal syndicate linked to Pakistan.

hindi_translation.headline: मुंबई में संवेदनशील स्थानों की रेकी करने के आरोप में युवक गिरफ्तार, विदेशी आपराधिक गिरोह से जुड़े तार
hindi_translation.story_lead: नवी मुंबई के ऐरोली निवासी 20 वर्षीय युवक को दक्षिण मुंबई में चाबाड हाउस सहित अन्य संवेदनशील स्थलों की निगरानी और रेकी करने के आरोप में गिरफ्तार किया गया है। आरोपी विदेशी आपराधिक गिरोहों और देशविरोधी तत्वों के निर्देशों पर काम कर रहा था। महाराष्ट्र आतंकवाद निरोधी दस्ते (ATS) द्वारा हिरासत में लिए जाने के बाद उसे UAPA मामले में केरल पुलिस को सौंप दिया गया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
दक्षिण मुंबई में महत्वपूर्ण और संवेदनशील प्रतिष्ठानों की निगरानी करने तथा उनकी तस्वीरें लेने के आरोप में 20 वर्षीय यश सिंह नाम के युवक को गिरफ्तार किया गया है। महाराष्ट्र आतंकवाद निरोधी दस्ते (ATS) की शुरुआती जांच में पता चला कि वह सोशल मीडिया के जरिए विदेशी आपराधिक नेटवर्क और देशविरोधी आकाओं के संपर्क में था। पूछताछ के बाद सिंह को केरल पुलिस के हवाले कर दिया गया, जहां त्रिशूर ईस्ट पुलिस स्टेशन में गैरकानूनी गतिविधियां (रोकथाम) अधिनियम (UAPA) के तहत दर्ज मामले में उसकी संलिप्तता की पुष्टि हुई।

आधिकारिक बयानों के अनुसार, आरोपी को पाकिस्तान स्थित 'शहजाद भट्टी नेटवर्क' जैसे अंतरराष्ट्रीय माफिया गिरोहों से जुड़े ऑनलाइन आकाओं द्वारा निर्देश दिए जा रहे थे। उसका काम दक्षिण मुंबई के कोलाबा क्षेत्र में चाबाड हाउस, यहूदी नागरिकों के स्वामित्व वाले व्यवसायों और विदेशी पर्यटकों की आवाजाही वाले क्षेत्रों की तस्वीरें खींचना तथा सटीक स्थान का नक्शा तैयार करना था। इन गतिविधियों के बदले उसे वित्तीय भुगतान किया गया था।

जांच से यह भी स्पष्ट हुआ कि आरोपी टेलीग्राम जैसे एनक्रिप्टेड मैसेजिंग प्लेटफॉर्म के जरिए संपर्क में था। विदेशी आपराधिक गिरोह टेलीग्राम, इंस्टाग्राम और व्हाट्सएप जैसे सोशल मीडिया प्लेटफॉर्म का उपयोग बेरोजगार और आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर युवाओं को पैसों का लालच देकर रेकी और विध्वंसकारी गतिविधियों में शामिल करने के लिए कर रहे हैं। एटीएस ने नागरिकों और अभिभावकों को सतर्क रहने तथा किसी भी अज्ञात ऑनलाइन संपर्क से दूरी बनाए रखने की सलाह दी है।
hindi_translation.background_context: दक्षिण मुंबई के कोलाबा स्थित चाबाड हाउस 2008 के 26/11 मुंबई आतंकी हमलों के दौरान पाकिस्तानी आतंकवादियों के प्रमुख लक्ष्यों में से एक था।
bullet_points: नवी मुंबई के 20 वर्षीय यश सिंह को संवेदनशील स्थानों की रेकी के आरोप में गिरफ्तार किया गया।
आरोपी ने कोलाबा में चाबाड हाउस, यहूदी व्यवसायों और विदेशी पर्यटकों के स्थानों की निगरानी की।
महाराष्ट्र ATS की खुफिया जानकारी के आधार पर शुरुआती कार्रवाई की गई।

news.headline: NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava Spotlights India's Environmental Jurisprudence at COP17 in Armenia

### Overview of India's Representation at COP17
National Green Tribunal (NGT) Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava addressed delegates at the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) held in Armenia. In his address, Justice Shrivastava emphasized India's proactive legal framework and pioneering judicial mechanisms in protecting the environment, framing them as key contributions to international environmental law.

### Key Highlights
- **Leadership in Legal Precedents:** The NGT Chairperson pointed out how Indian legal decisions and specialized tribunal mechanisms have created effective precedents for environmental conservation and sustainable development globally.
- **Forum and Location:** The discussions took place during the COP17 proceedings hosted in Armenia, gathering global legal experts, environmentalists, and state representatives to discuss international environmental governance.

The address highlighted India's key contributions to global environmental jurisprudence.

The summit brought together international stakeholders to discuss global environmental policy and governance framework.

hindi_translation.story_lead: राष्ट्रीय हरित अधिकरण (NGT) के अध्यक्ष न्यायमूर्ति प्रकाश श्रीवास्तव ने आर्मेनिया में आयोजित COP17 सम्मेलन में भारत का प्रतिनिधित्व किया। इस सम्मेलन के दौरान, उन्होंने वैश्विक पर्यावरणीय न्यायशास्त्र में देश की महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका और योगदान पर जोर दिया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### COP17 में भारत के प्रतिनिधित्व का अवलोकन
राष्ट्रीय हरित अधिकरण (NGT) के अध्यक्ष न्यायमूर्ति प्रकाश श्रीवास्तव ने आर्मेनिया में आयोजित पक्षकारों के 17वें सम्मेलन (COP17) को संबोधित किया। अपने संबोधन में, न्यायमूर्ति श्रीवास्तव ने पर्यावरण की रक्षा में भारत के सक्रिय कानूनी ढांचे और अग्रणी न्यायिक तंत्रों पर प्रकाश डाला, और इन्हें अंतर्राष्ट्रीय पर्यावरण कानून में प्रमुख योगदान के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया।

### मुख्य बिंदु
- **कानूनी मिसालों में नेतृत्व:** एनजीटी अध्यक्ष ने इस बात पर बल दिया कि कैसे भारतीय कानूनी निर्णयों और विशेष न्यायाधिकरण तंत्रों ने वैश्विक स्तर पर पर्यावरण संरक्षण और सतत विकास के लिए प्रभावी मिसालें कायम की हैं।
- **मंच और स्थान:** यह चर्चा आर्मेनिया में आयोजित COP17 की कार्यवाही के दौरान हुई, जिसमें वैश्विक कानूनी विशेषज्ञों, पर्यावरणविदों और राज्य प्रतिनिधियों ने अंतर्राष्ट्रीय पर्यावरण शासन पर चर्चा की।

शिखर सम्मेलन में वैश्विक पर्यावरण नीति पर चर्चा के लिए अंतर्राष्ट्रीय हितधारक एकत्र हुए।

news.headline: HT Leadership Summit: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz questions value of trade deals with Trump’s US
news.story_lead: HT Leadership Summit: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz questions value of trade deals with Trump’s US Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz said Trump “just doesn’t understand what to do”, citing coffee taxation Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz on Saturday questioned what a trade deal with the US was worth under President Donald Trump. He said Canada’s agreement with Washington had done little good. Stiglitz cited the EU example and said the US was pressing its trading partners to give up their sovereignty.
news.full_article_text: HT Leadership Summit: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz questions value of trade deals with Trump’s US Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz said Trump “just doesn’t understand what to do”, citing coffee taxation Nobel laureate economist Joseph E Stiglitz on Saturday questioned what a trade deal with the US was worth under President Donald Trump. He said Canada’s agreement with Washington had done little good. Stiglitz cited the EU example and said the US was pressing its trading partners to give up their sovereignty. “Canada had a trade agreement with the US. What good did it do?” Stiglitz said at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in conversation with Dr Niranjan Rajadhyaksha, executive director of Artha Global. He pointed to Europe’s attempt to control its digital economy and the worrying US response. “And the US said no, not if you are trading with us. And then you are giving up your sovereignty. That is something to be worried about,” said Stiglitz, who chaired Bill Clinton’s Council of Economic Advisers from 1995 to 1997 and was the World Bank’s chief economist (1997 to 2000). Deep Dive Stiglitz said Trump’s tariffs would not bring production back to the US. He added that Trump “just doesn’t understand what to do”, citing coffee taxation. “Taxing coffee does not bring coffee production. We [US] don’t have the weather for it,” said Stiglitz, who shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in economics. His remarks came on the same morning that external affairs minister S Jaishankar said at the summit that India and the US had sorted out the bulk of issues in their trade talks and reached the finishing line. In a column in July, Stiglitz wrote that when another country has the means and the willingness to fight back, Trump “always chickens out”.

news.headline: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
news.story_lead: The lower stage of the rocket was diverted to the ocean as it burst into flames - Published 13 November 2026 SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage at about 15:15 local time (21:15 GMT) on Saturday.
news.full_article_text: The lower stage of the rocket was diverted to the ocean as it burst into flames - Published 13 November 2026 SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage at about 15:15 local time (21:15 GMT) on Saturday. It is the company's first attempt to fully recover its rocket, paving the way for making Starship fully reusable so it can fly repeatedly and reduce costs. Starship is the tallest and most powerful rocket ever built The 124m-tall rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 16:45 local time (22:45 GMT) on Friday. It was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six and a half minutes later when it returned to the launch tower, but instead it was diverted to the ocean. During a stream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each maneuver safely." The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet from space. The Ship is due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower 22.5 hours after taking off, where a second catch may be attempted. SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead, it has splashed down in the ocean. Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it is in space. If any problems are detected, there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. news.headline: India's Border Capability Improved Significantly Despite Active Border Dynamics, Says EAM S. Jaishankar
news.story_lead: Speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi, External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar stated that India's border with China has become 'more alive', but emphasized that Indian force sustainment and infrastructure capabilities along the frontier have significantly improved over the last decade. He also noted that while India and China had comparable economic scales in the 1980s, China rapidly industrialized while India missed that development phase.
news.full_article_text:
Addressing the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit (HTLS 2026) in New Delhi, External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar reflected on the evolving security and economic dynamics between India and China. He noted that the border with China has become 'more alive in a way,' but highlighted that India's capacity to deploy and sustain armed forces along the frontier has experienced substantial enhancement. According to Jaishankar, border infrastructure had suffered from systemic neglect until roughly ten years ago, after which a deliberate policy shift led to major operational improvements.

Contextualizing the operational environment, the External Affairs Minister alluded to the violent June 2020 Galwan Valley clash, which resulted in the deaths of 20 Indian soldiers and unconfirmed casualties on the Chinese side. The incident severely damaged bilateral diplomatic relations, bringing them to a historical low.

In addition to security matters, Jaishankar drew a direct comparison between the historical economic trajectories of the two nations. He highlighted that when Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi visited China in 1988, both economies were roughly equivalent in size. However, China undertook an aggressive push toward industrialization and modernization throughout the 1980s, whereas India failed to capitalize on industrial development during the same period, creating a long-term economic gap between the two neighbours.
news.background_context: Bilateral relations between India and China plummeted following a violent military face-off in the Galwan Valley in June 2020, which caused the deaths of 20 Indian personnel and an unspecified number of Chinese troops.
bullet_points: External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar addressed the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi.
He characterized the border with China as having become 'more alive in a way'.
He emphasized that India's capability to deploy and sustain forces along the frontier has improved significantly.
Border infrastructure was neglected until roughly a decade ago, according to the minister.
The 2020 Galwan Valley clash brought India-China bilateral relations to a new low.
India and China had similar economic sizes during Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's 1988 visit to China.
China executed a massive modernization and industrialization push during the 1980s.
India missed the industrialization push during the 1980s, widening the economic divide with China.

June 2020: Violent military clash in Galwan Valley.

GS Paper III: Border area security management, infrastructure development, and defense preparedness.
news.upsc_analysis: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's statements highlight two crucial strategic dimensions: defense preparedness along contested borders and the strategic consequences of economic industrialization. The shift from past neglect of frontier infrastructure to active operational enhancements since 2014 reflects India's proactive deterrence strategy post-Galwan 2020. Simultaneously, the historic comparison of 1980s economic trajectories emphasizes that long-term strategic weight and defense capabilities are heavily underpinned by industrial capacity.
causes: Systemic neglect of border infrastructure prior to a decade ago.
Divergent economic policies in the 1980s, where China focused heavily on industrialization while India lagged behind.
The June 2020 Galwan Valley violent clash, which fundamentally altered border security posture.
impacts: Significant enhancement in India's force deployment and sustainment capacity along the LAC.
Heightened operational alertness along an increasingly active frontier.
Widened structural economic gap between India and China stemming from 1980s industrial policies.
challenges: Maintaining long-term border stability and deterrence along an active frontier.
Overcoming historical manufacturing and industrial gaps relative to China.
government_steps: Focused development and modernization of border infrastructure over the past decade to enhance troop sustainment.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Relates to India's National Security Strategy and Ministry of External Affairs policy frameworks on border management and neighborhood diplomacy.
way_forward: Sustaining momentum in border logistics and infrastructure development while pursuing calibrated economic industrialization to support long-term national security capabilities.
news.mains_notes:
Key Takeaways on India-China Relations:
1. Border Posture: Border infrastructure underwent minimal development until a decade ago. Post-2014 developments and the 2020 Galwan clash (20 Indian casualties) led to significantly enhanced deployment and logistical capabilities.
2. Economic Divergence: In 1988 (PM Rajiv Gandhi's visit), India and China held equivalent economic scales. China's focused industrialization in the 1980s created the present economic asymmetry between both nations.

hindi_translation.story_lead: नई दिल्ली में 24वें हिंदुस्तान टाइम्स लीडरशिप समिट को संबोधित करते हुए विदेश मंत्री डॉ. एस. जयशंकर ने कहा कि चीन के साथ भारत की सीमा 'एक तरह से अधिक जीवंत' हो गई है, लेकिन इस बात पर जोर दिया कि पिछले एक दशक में सीमा पर भारतीय बलों की तैनाती और बुनियादी ढांचे की क्षमताओं में उल्लेखनीय सुधार हुआ है। उन्होंने यह भी कहा कि जहां 1980 के दशक में भारत और चीन की अर्थव्यवस्थाओं का आकार समान था, वहीं चीन ने तेजी से औद्योगीकरण किया जबकि भारत उस विकास चरण से चूक गया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
नई दिल्ली में 24वें हिंदुस्तान टाइम्स लीडरशिप समिट (HTLS 2026) को संबोधित करते हुए विदेश मंत्री डॉ. एस. जयशंकर ने भारत और चीन के बीच बदलते सुरक्षा और आर्थिक संबंधों पर विचार साझा किए। उन्होंने टिप्पणी की कि चीन के साथ सीमा 'एक तरह से अधिक सक्रिय' हो गई है, लेकिन इस बात पर प्रकाश डाला कि सीमा पर सशस्त्र बलों को तैनात करने और बनाए रखने की भारत की क्षमता में भारी वृद्धि हुई है। जयशंकर के अनुसार, लगभग एक दशक पहले तक सीमावर्ती बुनियादी ढांचे की उपेक्षा की गई थी, जिसके बाद एक लक्षित नीतिगत बदलाव से परिचालन क्षमताओं में बड़ा सुधार आया।

परिचालन वातावरण का संदर्भ देते हुए, विदेश मंत्री ने जून 2020 की गलवान घाटी की हिंसक झड़प का उल्लेख किया, जिसमें 20 भारतीय सैनिक शहीद हो गए थे और चीनी पक्ष में अनिर्दिष्ट हताहत हुए थे। इस घटना ने द्विपक्षीय राजनयिक संबंधों को गंभीर नुकसान पहुंचाया और वे ऐतिहासिक निचले स्तर पर पहुंच गए।

सुरक्षा मामलों के अलावा, जयशंकर ने दोनों देशों के ऐतिहासिक आर्थिक प्रक्षेपवक्र की प्रत्यक्ष तुलना की। उन्होंने रेखांकित किया कि जब प्रधानमंत्री राजीव गांधी ने 1988 में चीन का दौरा किया था, तब दोनों अर्थव्यवस्थाएं आकार में लगभग बराबर थीं। हालांकि, चीन ने 1980 के दशक के दौरान औद्योगीकरण और आधुनिकीकरण की दिशा में आक्रामक प्रयास किया, जबकि भारत उसी अवधि के दौरान औद्योगिक विकास का लाभ उठाने में विफल रहा, जिससे दोनों पड़ोसियों के बीच एक दीर्घकालिक आर्थिक अंतर पैदा हो गया।

news.headline: EAM S. Jaishankar Outlines Foreign Policy Blueprint Driven by Domestic Manufacturing and Frontier Technologies
news.story_lead: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar detailed a strategic framework for navigating a shifting global order during the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi. He emphasized that domestic economic initiatives like Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India serve as the core building blocks of India's foreign policy. To maintain strategic autonomy, India must bridge historical manufacturing gaps while accelerating investments in emerging technologies like AI and semiconductors.
news.full_article_text:
### Foreign Policy Built on Domestic Economic Capacity

Speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi, themed "New Rules. New Realities.", External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated that domestic flagship economic programs—including Atmanirbhar Bharat, Make in India, and Innovate in India—are fundamental building blocks of Indian foreign policy rather than standalone economic initiatives. In an interactive session with R. Sukumar, Editor-in-Chief of Hindustan Times, the minister highlighted that an effective external strategy in the contemporary era relies directly on robust national capabilities.

### Overcoming Historical Manufacturing Shortfalls

Jaishankar noted that while India has created a strong foundation over the past decade, the country historically "missed the manufacturing bus" during the period spanning the 1960s to the 1990s, describing those years as lost decades. He added that the economic reforms of 1991–92 acted only as a partial correction. To overcome these historical deficits, the government is utilizing targeted policy instruments such as the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme to reinvigorate neglected industries, support small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and enhance physical infrastructure alongside logistics networks.

### Strategic Investments in Frontier Technologies

To ensure long-term competitiveness in an evolving geopolitical landscape, the minister outlined the necessity of expanding domestic capabilities across frontier sectors. Key priorities include scaling up research and manufacturing in semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), and bio-life sciences. Additionally, strengthening educational institutions and expanding vocational skilling are critical to preparing the workforce for an AI-driven global economy.

### Navigating a Transactional Global Order

Addressing geopolitical trends, Jaishankar observed that traditional international alliances are becoming less cohesive and increasingly transactional. As global dynamics shift toward self-centred competition among nation-states, building internal strength across technology, manufacturing, and supply chain logistics becomes essential to maintaining strategic autonomy and effective global engagement.

hindi_translation.story_lead: विदेश मंत्री एस. जयशंकर ने नई दिल्ली में आयोजित 24वें हिंदुस्तान टाइम्स लीडरशिप समिट के दौरान वैश्विक व्यवस्था में बदलाव से निपटने के लिए एक बहुस्तरीय रणनीति प्रस्तुत की। उन्होंने जोर दिया कि 'आत्मनिर्भर भारत' और 'मेक इन इंडिया' जैसी आर्थिक पहल केवल आर्थिक नीतियां नहीं हैं, बल्कि भारत की विदेश नीति के मुख्य आधार हैं।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### घरेलू आर्थिक क्षमता पर आधारित विदेश नीति

नई दिल्ली में "न्यू रूल्स. न्यू रियलिटीज." थीम के तहत आयोजित 24वें हिंदुस्तान टाइम्स लीडरशिप समिट में बोलते हुए, विदेश मंत्री एस. जयशंकर ने कहा कि आत्मनिर्भर भारत, मेक इन इंडिया और इनोवेट इन इंडिया जैसे प्रमुख आर्थिक कार्यक्रम विदेश नीति के बुनियादी निर्माण खंड हैं। उन्होंने स्पष्ट किया कि इस दौर में एक प्रभावी विदेश नीति मजबूत राष्ट्रीय क्षमताओं के बिना संभव नहीं है।

### ऐतिहासिक विनिर्माण घाटे को पूरा करना

जयशंकर ने उल्लेख किया कि भारत ने पिछले दशक में एक मजबूत नींव रखी है, लेकिन देश 1960 के दशक से 1990 के दशक के दौरान विनिर्माण क्षेत्र में पिछड़ गया था, जिसे उन्होंने 'खोए हुए दशक' करार दिया। उन्होंने कहा कि 1991-92 के आर्थिक सुधार केवल आंशिक सुधार थे। इस अंतर को समाप्त करने के लिए सरकार प्रोडक्शन-लिंक्ड इंसेंटिव (PLI) जैसी योजनाओं का उपयोग कर रही है ताकि उपेक्षित उद्योगों और छोटे तथा मध्यम उद्यमों (SMEs) को बढ़ावा दिया जा सके।

### उभरती प्रौद्योगिकियों में रणनीतिक निवेश

बदलते भू-राजनीतिक परिदृश्य में प्रतिस्पर्धात्मक बने रहने के लिए, मंत्री ने सेमीकंडक्टर, आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस (AI) और बायो-लाइफ साइंसेज जैसे उभरते क्षेत्रों में घरेलू क्षमताओं को बढ़ाने की आवश्यकता पर बल दिया। इसके अतिरिक्त, AI-संचालित अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए कार्यबल को तैयार करने हेतु शैक्षणिक संस्थानों और व्यावसायिक कौशल का विस्तार करना आवश्यक है।

### लेन-देन पर आधारित वैश्विक व्यवस्था में नेविगेशन

वैश्विक भू-राजनीति के संदर्भ में, जयशंकर ने कहा कि पारंपरिक गठबंधन कम एकजुट और अधिक लेन-देन पर आधारित हो रहे हैं। जैसे-जैसे वैश्विक स्थितियां राष्ट्रों के बीच आक्रामक प्रतिस्पर्धा की ओर बढ़ रही हैं, रणनीतिक स्वायत्तता बनाए रखने के लिए प्रौद्योगिकी और विनिर्माण में आंतरिक क्षमताएं मजबूत करना अनिवार्य हो गया है।

news.story_lead: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh paid tribute to India's first Prime Minister, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, on his 137th birth anniversary on November 14. Celebrated across India as National Children's Day or 'Bal Diwas', the day commemorates Nehru's legacy, his role in the freedom struggle, and his deep affection for children.
news.full_article_text:
### Tributes Paid to India's First Prime Minister
On November 14, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh commemorated the 137th birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru. PM Modi extended his tributes through an official statement on X, recognizing Nehru's lasting contributions to the nation. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh highlighted Nehru's crucial involvement in India's freedom struggle and his leadership during the crucial founding years of independent India.

### Origins and Significance of National Children's Day
Across India, November 14 is celebrated annually as National Children's Day, locally known as 'Bal Diwas'. Jawaharlal Nehru, affectionately referred to as 'Chacha Nehru', was renowned for his deep fondness for children and his emphasis on child welfare and education. Born on November 14, 1889, in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, Nehru took office as the first Prime Minister of independent India on August 15, 1947, serving until his passing on May 27, 1964.

Following his death in May 1964, the Parliament of India unanimously adopted a resolution designating his birth anniversary as National Children's Day. Prior to this shift, India had observed Children's Day on November 20, coinciding with the Universal Children's Day established by the United Nations in 1954. Educational institutions nationwide celebrate the occasion with student competitions, sports, and cultural programmes, while political leaders and institutional heads, including President Droupadi Murmu, host commemorative events.
news.background_context: Initially, India celebrated Children's Day on November 20 following the United Nations declaration of Universal Children's Day in 1954. Following the death of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on May 27, 1964, the Indian Parliament passed a unanimous resolution to shift National Children's Day to November 14 to honor his life and love for children.

government_steps: Parliament of India passed a unanimous resolution in 1964 declaring November 14 as National Children's Day.
Government bodies and constitutional heads organize nation-wide commemorative events and student interaction programs.
news.mains_notes: Jawaharlal Nehru served as India's prime minister from 1947 to 1964, shaping early post-independence governance and foreign policy. hindi_translation.headline: देश ने जवाहरलाल नेहरू की 137वीं जयंती पर राष्ट्रीय बाल दिवस मनाया
hindi_translation.story_lead: प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी और रक्षा मंत्री राजनाथ सिंह ने 14 नवंबर को भारत के प्रथम प्रधानमंत्री पंडित जवाहरलाल नेहरू की 137वीं जयंती पर उन्हें श्रद्धांजलि अर्पित की। देश भर में 'बाल दिवस' के रूप में मनाए जाने वाले इस दिन नेहरू के योगदान और बच्चों के प्रति उनके प्रेम को याद किया जाता है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### देश के प्रथम प्रधानमंत्री को श्रद्धांजलि
14 नवंबर को प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी और रक्षा मंत्री राजनाथ सिंह ने पंडित जवाहरलाल नेहरू की 137वीं जयंती पर उन्हें नमन किया। पीएम मोदी ने एक्स (X) पर पोस्ट के माध्यम से पूर्व पीएम को श्रद्धांजलि दी। वहीं रक्षा मंत्री राजनाथ सिंह ने स्वतंत्रता संग्राम और स्वतंत्र भारत के शुरुआती वर्षों में नेहरू के नेतृत्व और योगदान को याद किया।

### राष्ट्रीय बाल दिवस का इतिहास और महत्व
भारत भर में हर साल 14 नवंबर को राष्ट्रीय बाल दिवस (बाल दिवस) के रूप में मनाया जाता है। जवाहरलाल नेहरू, जिन्हें बच्चे प्यार से 'चाचा नेहरू' कहते थे, बच्चों के प्रति अपने विशेष स्नेह और उनके कल्याण पर जोर देने के लिए जाने जाते थे। 14 नवंबर 1889 को उत्तर प्रदेश के प्रयागराज में जन्मे नेहरू 15 अगस्त 1947 को स्वतंत्र भारत के पहले प्रधानमंत्री बने और 27 मई 1964 तक इस पद पर रहे।

मई 1964 में उनके निधन के बाद, भारतीय संसद ने सर्वसम्मति से उनकी जयंती को राष्ट्रीय बाल दिवस के रूप में मनाने का संकल्प पारित किया। इससे पहले भारत 1954 में संयुक्त राष्ट्र द्वारा घोषित सार्वभौमिक बाल दिवस के अनुसार 20 नवंबर को बाल दिवस मनाता था। इस अवसर पर देशभर के स्कूलों में खेल, प्रतियोगिताएं और सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रम आयोजित किए जाते हैं।
